title: Execution-graph snapshot and loop quarantine for multi-tool flows
creator: Aisha Park
description: Prevent unbounded recursion and unsafe state injection in multi-tool execution loops while preserving streaming and structured-output UX. Add lightweight execution-graph snapshots and a quarantine mode that isolates suspicious call-chains and degrades to deterministic fallbacks. This ticket covers design, implementation, and rollout for server-side snapshotting, loop-detection heuristics, token-budget gating, and developer-visible provenance headers for debugging.
technical_notes: We will capture a compact execution-graph snapshot at tool invocation boundaries: caller node id, tool id, input digest (sha256), parent chain length, and a provenance token. Snapshots are immutable, short-lived, stored in in-memory ring with TTL (default 30s). Loop detection uses a combination of: repeated tool id within same chain, repeated input digest, and parent chain length > configurable threshold (default 8). When a loop is detected, mark the chain as QUARANTINED and route subsequent calls to quarantine handlers: 1) deterministic fallback model variant (compatibility layer), 2) stubbed tool response if available, or 3) abort with structured error explaining provenance and remediation. Streaming responses must still flush any buffered tokens produced prior to quarantine; quarantine only affects future tool calls. We will tag all tool responses with provenance headers: X-RI-Prov: <token>, X-RI-Chain-Len: <n>, X-RI-Quarantine: true|false. Quarantine decisions are logged to a separate high-cardinality metric and a sampled debug sink for 1% of events. The implementation will be in three parts: snapshot layer (lightweight ring), detection engine (configurable rules), and quarantine router (fallbacks + telemetry).
acceptance_criteria: 1) Execution-graph snapshots are emitted for every tool call in staging and can be queried by token. 2) The system detonates into quarantine for nested loops according to heuristics and uses deterministic fallback variants for hosted models. 3) Streaming responses flush pre-quarantine tokens and subsequent tool calls are prevented. 4) Provenance headers appear on responses and match the snapshot state. 5) System-level metrics (quarantine_count, quarantine_rate, average_chain_length_at_quarantine) are available in Console. 6) Integration tests simulate recursive tool chains and assert quarantine and graceful degradation behaviors.
rollout_plan: Phase 1: feature-flag rollout to internal dev org; snapshot TTL=30s, loop threshold=8, quarantine sampling enabled. Phase 2: opt-in for select customers (beta) with runtime-1.22. Phase 3: gradual default-on after 3 weeks and monitoring thresholds stable. Emergency rollback: disable quarantine routing and revert to pre-snapshot routing with a 1-hour config flip. Communicate to customers via release notes and Console banner during beta.
QA_test_cases: Simple tool chain: ToolA -> ToolB -> response unchanged; assert no quarantine
Recursive call: ToolX calls ToolX repeatedly; assert quarantine after threshold and deterministic fallback used
Input-reuse detection: same input digest across different tools; ensure we do not false-positive quarantine below threshold
Streaming flush: streaming tokens produced before quarantine are delivered; subsequent tool-calls blocked
Provenance header integrity: headers map to snapshot store entries
Performance: snapshot write/read latency < 500us under 1k rps per runtime instance
review_feedback: PM (Maya Chen): prefer making the loop threshold configurable per-customer; avoid hard fail for enterprise customers during beta
Security (Ethan Brooks): ensure provenance token entropy >= 128 bits and do not leak raw inputs in logs; redact where necessary
Design (Olivia Reed): show quarantine state in the Console timeline for affected requests to help debugging
Infra (Noah Patel): prefer ring buffer with preallocated slots to avoid GC pressure; test mem usage under 10k concurrent chains
